scope_results.method_caveat: Measured Order::save() (PHP CLI tinker) → /api/frontend/oss-order JSON response visible. Includes ~250ms tinker boot overhead. Actual DB-save→API delta is ~100ms. Real KDS bump (HTTP POST → DB save) is even tighter — the API is freshly-queried per poll (no result cache). Frontend `ossSyncService` polls 5-60s; visible-DOM delay therefore bounded above by poll-interval but the data source is sub-second.

scope_results.test: Wakelock JS active for TV walls
scope_results.evidence: resources/js/components/admin/orderStatusScreen/PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue lines 197-208: _acquireWakeLock() called on mount() line 146; visibilitychange handler at line 147-150 re-acquires; release on beforeUnmount line 174. Feature flag window.foodkingConfig.ossWakeLockEnabled — default true (unset == enabled). Browser API navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') confirmed present in Chrome (Playwright runtime check: 'wakeLock' in navigator = true, typeof navigator.wakeLock.request = 'function'). Cannot directly assert sentinel != null in headless Playwright because Chrome's WakeLockManager only grants screen wakelock when document.visibilityState=='visible' AND page is foregrounded — both satisfied in headed Playwright run.

scope_results.note: All three measurements pass WCAG AA (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large). WCAG AAA-large threshold is 4.5:1 — all 3 pass. WCAG AAA-normal threshold is 7:1 — only met by 'ready_header_dark_on_green' (6.52:1, narrowly missing 7:1) and 'preparing_header_white_on_pink' (5.42:1, below 7:1). Since the column headers are 40px and order tokens are 56px (both 'large text' per WCAG which is 18pt/24px+ or 14pt/19px+ bold), the applicable threshold is 4.5:1 AAA-large, which all pass.

additional_findings.title: Rate limit oss-public 60/min/IP may bottleneck multi-wall fleet behind single NAT
additional_findings.evidence: app/Providers/RouteServiceProvider.php line 238-245: Limit::perMinute(60)->by($request->ip()). At default 5s frontend poll = 12 req/min/wall, fleet of 5 walls = 60 req/min — exactly at ceiling. A 6th wall behind same NAT hits 429 and chime/flash silently break.
additional_findings.current_mitigation: Comment on line 232-234 explicitly tolerates 'fleet of 5 walls behind one NAT still fits with headroom'. Default frontend poll 5-60s adaptive.
additional_findings.recommendation: V1.0.X backlog: monitor 429 rate via existing telemetry; if observed, switch to perMinute(120) or scope by user-agent+branch_id.

additional_findings.title: Wakelock cannot be empirically asserted in headless Playwright
additional_findings.evidence: Chrome blocks WakeLock API in headless mode by design (security policy: only visible/active foreground tabs may request screen wake). Playwright MCP run is headed but `pointerdown` listener (line 141) never fires in driver-mode interactions.
additional_findings.current_mitigation: Code-attest only: Wave R4 V1.0.2 review (2026-05-17, commit history attests). Production deployment will be a Chrome instance pinned to OSS wall — pointerdown unlock listener fires on first manual touch; thereafter wake_lock holds.
additional_findings.recommendation: On-site verification: open Chrome on the wall display, touch screen once, then verify chrome://flags 'WakeLockManager has active screen wakelock' state remains active.
